cap: Male development is a chain of signals: SRY makes a testis, Sertoli cells make AMH, Leydig cells make testosterone, and 5-alpha-reductase makes dihydrotestosterone (DHT) for the external genitalia. Swyer syndrome breaks the first link, 5-alpha-reductase deficiency breaks the DHT link and androgen insensitivity breaks the receptor link, while congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) and aromatase deficiency add androgen to a 46,XX fetus.
teach: Read down the chain and stop at the broken link; everything above it works and everything below it fails. A uterus means no AMH was made, so the testis itself is missing, as in Swyer syndrome. No uterus with female genitalia means the testis worked but androgen could not act, as in androgen insensitivity.
